clusters.title: Set up and start a task
clusters.lead: Connect a provider, link your tools and begin from an issue, a workflow or a question.

items.title: Welcome to Goodboy
items.text: Five short steps take you from install to a first agent reading your project. Skip any step that does not apply to you.

items.title: Provider connection
items.text: Connect the provider you already use with a login or an API key. Each card shows whether it is connected, signed out or missing.

items.title: One page per provider
items.text: Each provider has its own page for usage, which models appear in the picker, permissions and your account.

items.title: Update the provider CLI
items.text: A banner tells you when a model needs a newer provider tool. One button updates it once running turns finish.

items.title: Permissions for each provider
items.text: See which permission modes a provider can honor before you pick one. A mode it cannot honor never runs looser.

items.title: Integrations
items.text: Connect GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Linear, Jira, Sentry and Slack from one page. Keys stay in your system credential store.

items.title: About you
items.text: Tell agents once who you are and how you like to work. You can see which role reads each part.

items.title: How do you want to start?
items.text: A new session draft offers three tabs: pick up a task, run a workflow or ask an agent. It becomes a session only when you press Start.

items.title: Pick up a task, with a drafted brief
items.text: Pick an issue and Goodboy drafts a short title, a goal and done-when criteria. Keep the brief, edit it or use the issue text.

items.title: Run a workflow
items.text: Write a goal, choose how steps are picked and read the plan before you run it. One press creates the session and starts the run.

items.title: Ask an agent
items.text: Map an unfamiliar repo before you plan. The scout only reads, so it changes nothing.

items.title: Start blank
items.text: Start from the goal instead. A blank session opens on its overview, where you add the goal, projects and work.

items.title: Named by Goodboy
items.text: A new session gets a short title without you writing one. It is marked until you rename it.

items.title: Settings rail
items.text: Each settings area says what needs you, like folders not found.

clusters.title: Follow a task while it runs
clusters.lead: See what needs you from any screen, find anything fast, and watch each session move across the board.

items.title: Session overview
items.text: Find the goal, linked issues, projects, cost and the buttons to start an agent on one screen. Each project lists its branches and pull request state.

items.title: Refresh a session
items.text: Pull requests made outside Goodboy show up when a turn ends or you come back to the window. Refresh re-reads everything right away.

items.title: Activity
items.text: Read the whole session as one timeline of agents, questions, fixes, pull requests and decisions. Related steps fold into a single row.

items.title: Next
items.text: Goodboy shows the one move that unblocks a task, like answering a question or opening a pull request. Put a suggestion away until things change.

items.title: Time left
items.text: Queued steps show how long they should take, learned from your own past runs. Thin history shows a count instead of a guess.

items.title: File versions
items.text: Undo an agent's edit without a branch. Each changed file is kept as it was, with a Restore button.

items.title: Activity bar
items.text: A bar on the left lists the sessions of the workspace by where they stand. Each row says what it is waiting on.

items.title: Now chip
items.text: A chip in the top bar counts sessions that need you and those running. Click it to jump straight to one.

items.title: Notifications
items.text: Everything Goodboy has to tell you lands in one list with an unread count. A row that needs you carries its next step.

items.title: Open in new window
items.text: Give each workspace its own window so switching never interrupts running agents. Windows come back as you left them after a restart.

items.title: Go anywhere
items.text: Press ⌘K and type a few letters to find any session, agent, plan, page or script. Enter opens it.

items.title: Command palette
items.text: Act on what you are looking at. The actions of the open agent and session come first, each with its shortcut.

items.title: Search
items.text: Find a message, plan, decision, issue or branch with ⌘F, starting in the open session. The index stays on your computer.

items.title: Right click menus
items.text: Right click almost anything to see every action it has. The menu and the palette list the same actions in the same order.

items.title: Stage board
items.text: See where each session stands without moving cards. Each one sits in building, running, needs you or in review.

items.title: Session card
items.text: Read a task at a glance: pull request or status, agent count, project, cost and age. A round button opens a waiting action.

items.title: Done and Archived dock
items.text: Finished sessions fold into two icons at the side of the board. Click one to open its column.

items.title: Bulk select
items.text: Lasso or modifier-click cards across columns, then archive, restore or delete them together.

clusters.title: Shared context and projects
clusters.lead: What one agent learns, the next one reads, across every repo your work touches.

items.title: Decisions
items.text: Record a decision once and later agents read it. Replacing or withdrawing one needs a reason that stays next to it.

items.title: See why each decision was made
items.text: The reason behind a decision stays visible in the drawer, as a muted line under the decision itself.

items.title: Running summary
items.text: After each turn a summary of state, next steps, open questions and lessons is updated for the next agent. Your own edits are kept.

items.title: Context drawer
items.text: Open the goal, decisions and summary from any session page. Copy them out as a brief and see what changed since you last looked.

items.title: Context budgets
items.text: Prompts stay small as a session grows. Each part of the shared brief has its own size, and the newest decisions are kept.

items.title: Plans handed to the next agent
items.text: Hand a plan straight to the implementer. The plan moves from Ready to run to Ran and shows which agent used it.

items.title: Start a project from nothing
items.text: Begin with an empty folder. Goodboy starts the repository, a first session works in it, and Publish puts main on GitHub when you are ready.

items.title: Workspace with several projects
items.text: Keep your repos together and let one session work across several of them. A repo gets a branch only when an agent needs to edit it.

items.title: Starred projects, descriptions and base branch
items.text: Star a project and give it a one-line description, and agents read both in their brief. Starred projects come first in the pickers.

items.title: Worktrees
items.text: Each branch gets its own worktree, a separate folder next to your checkout. Agents edit in parallel without touching your own files.

items.title: Several branches per project
items.text: Work on several branches of one repo in the same session. If a worktree drifts to another branch, a card offers clear choices.

items.title: Workspace switcher and Reconnect
items.text: Jump between workspaces and projects from one search. Disconnecting keeps the history, and adding the folder again offers Reconnect.

items.title: Repo status across projects
items.text: See which repos are behind, uncommitted or diverged. Update the safe ones together, fast-forward only, and leave the rest to you.

items.title: Locate moved projects
items.text: If you moved your repos, pick the parent folder. Goodboy finds them again, fixes the paths and repairs the worktrees, with Undo move.

items.title: Keep .goodboy out of git
items.text: Keep Goodboy's own folder out of your commits with one click. The card shows only when git does not already ignore it.

clusters.title: Split work into steps
clusters.lead: Chain several agents in one run, each with its own role and model, and steer them as they go.

items.title: Workflow builder
items.text: Shape a run before it starts with a name, a goal and a mode. The plan is previewed as a recipe, step 1 on top, in the same nodes the run will show.

items.title: Orchestrated
items.text: Give a goal and a model picks each next step with a role, a model and a reason. It stops when done or blocked.

items.title: Preset and Custom
items.text: Write the steps yourself, or draft them with a planner. Save what you changed as a preset, or pick a saved one.

items.title: Built-in workflows
items.text: Start from Refactor, Plan and ship or Fix a bug. A built-in you delete stays deleted until you restore it.

items.title: Saved steps
items.text: Reuse steps across workflows. The built-in steps are read-only, and Save a copy makes your own.

items.title: Model per step
items.text: Put a light model on a scout and a strong one on the planner. Goodboy records what actually ran.

items.title: Autorun
items.text: Let a run move to its next step without you. A guard stops an agent after four unattended turns in an hour.

items.title: Spend limit
items.text: Cap what a run or a session can spend, then choose to pause workflows or only be warned. A paused run offers Raise limit.

items.title: Chained starts
items.text: Line work up behind work. A run can start now, wait for you, or start once another workflow completes.

items.title: Workflow run
items.text: Follow a run as a tree with one pinned next action. After a restart, one Resume all starts the stopped agents again.

items.title: Hints to the orchestrator
items.text: Steer a run while it goes. Queue a hint for the next decision, or read it now to stop the step in flight.

items.title: Why each step, and the run recap
items.text: See why each step was picked, with a short recap of what is done and what is left.

items.title: Step handoff summary
items.text: Each step starts from a short brief instead of the whole previous conversation. If the summary fails, the brief is marked degraded.

items.title: Open questions
items.text: Each question is one card: who asks, whether it blocks, and numbered answers with the recommended one tagged. Pick with a number key.

items.title: Let an agent decide
items.text: Hand a question to another agent with a hint and a model. Its answer counts as yours, and you can take it back.

items.title: Import workflows
items.text: Bring custom workflows over from your other workspaces with Import in the Workflows studio.

clusters.title: Review and branches
clusters.lead: Reshape history before it ships, turn comments into commits, and read your own diffs first.

items.title: Rewrite history
items.text: Clean up a branch by hand. Drag commits to move them, drop one onto another to fold it, or rename and remove them.

items.title: Safe apply
items.text: Your plan is tried on a temporary copy first, and a backup is saved before anything changes. If a step stops, your branch stays as it was.

items.title: Conflict prediction
items.text: While you edit the plan, Goodboy tries it in memory and marks each change that may conflict. Your checkout stays untouched.

items.title: Conflicts merged in a copy
items.text: When a step stops on a conflict, the notice names the step and the file. An agent can merge it in a copy, and Goodboy checks the result.

items.title: Push with lease and restore
items.text: Updating the online branch never overwrites a teammate's newer push. Restore takes the old history back, and the backup stays for 30 days.

items.title: Backups
items.text: Open the menu and choose Backups to see older histories of the branch. Restore previous history puts one back.

items.title: Suggest a message
items.text: Get a commit message drafted for a squash or a reword. Edit it before you apply.

items.title: Bring them into the plan
items.text: If someone pushed after you applied, Goodboy lists their new commits and offers to add them to the plan.

items.title: Rebase on main
items.text: Rebase on main with the same engine, and bring in an agent only when there is a conflict.

items.title: After a pull request merges
items.text: Choose what happens to a merged branch: ask me, delete on this Mac, or also on origin. You have 14 days to restore it.

items.title: Resolve
items.text: Turn review comments into commits without writing the fix yourself. Each comment gets its own agent, and you accept, edit or skip the result.

items.title: Review sources
items.text: One picker covers GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket and notes on your machine. Reading and replying work everywhere, and resolving works where the host allows it.

items.title: Comment states
items.text: Each comment shows what it needs next, such as not started, drafting, needs you, ready or done. A summary line counts them.

items.title: Failed drafts
items.text: A failed draft says why in plain words and links to the transcript. Try again, try another model or add a hint.

items.title: Manage a resolve from its Brief
items.text: Click a resolve in Activity to see the comment, the fix and the reply. Accept, edit, reply or skip, then push exactly that fix.

items.title: Fixes already on the branch
items.text: Review checks origin before it pushes. A fix already pushed, or one that someone else seems to have made, offers Reply and resolve instead.

items.title: A fix that went missing
items.text: If a fix commit is no longer on the branch, the comment says so. Goodboy checks git first, then can ask a read-only agent.

items.title: Close on GitHub
items.text: Finish a review in one action. Push sends the fixes, posts the replies and resolves the threads, after a confirm that counts them.

items.title: Review replies in your voice
items.text: Choose replies that sound like you: terse, friendly, formal, or learned from your last 20 replies. You can edit the style note.

items.title: Fixes on a branch that moved
items.text: Accept a fix even after the branch got new commits. It lands on top, and on a conflict the branch goes back to its old head.

items.title: Squash and fold the resolve commits
items.text: Choose how fixes land before anyone sees them. Keep them, fold each into its original commit, or make one commit for the review.

items.title: Notes before a pull request
items.text: Review your own diff first. Leave notes on lines, resolve them like review comments, and post the open ones to the pull request later.

items.title: GitHub pull request page
items.text: See in plain words whether a pull request can merge, with its checks. Merge, mark ready, draft or close it from there.

items.title: Pull request, Diff and Review as layers
items.text: Move between a pull request, its diff and its review without losing your place. Back walks the same path.

items.title: Write it for me
items.text: Get a pull request title, description and changelog entry in your repo's format. Linked issues become closing references.

items.title: PR description follows the push
items.text: A description Goodboy wrote is updated after a history push, unless you edited it.

items.title: Diff
items.text: Read changes with syntax colors, word-level highlights, a unified or split view and a viewed tick per file. Quote a line into a note or a question for an agent.

items.title: Write review
items.text: Review someone else's pull request in a form under the diff. Add line comments, pick comment, approve or request changes, and submit one review.

items.title: Written by Goodboy
items.text: Comments Goodboy posts end with a line that says so, and a setting turns it off.

items.title: Resolve again
items.text: Reread a comment and try the fix once more.

items.title: Checks
items.text: See a pull request's checks with their durations. A failed check becomes a suggested next step.

clusters.title: Inbox, plans and wireframes
clusters.lead: Connect your trackers once, let agents read them, and keep every document next to the task.

items.title: Supported tools
items.text: Connect GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Jira, Linear, Sentry and Slack in Settings. Each one feeds the Inbox and can start a session with its brief drafted.

items.title: Agents use your tools
items.text: Agents on any provider can read and act on your connected tools without ever holding your keys. Goodboy makes each call for them.

items.title: Inbox
items.text: Work from one list instead of seven tabs. Issues, Slack threads, Sentry errors and pull requests sit together, grouped by day.

items.title: Find any issue by code or link
items.text: Paste an issue code, a pull request number or a link to open it. It does not need to be assigned to you.

items.title: Starred issues
items.text: Star an issue to keep it on top of the Inbox and of the list you pick tasks from.

items.title: Launch a session from any item
items.text: Press Launch session on an issue, a Slack thread or an error. The session starts with its brief already drafted.

items.title: Link an item to a session
items.text: Attach an Inbox item to work that already exists. Link work in a session searches every connected tracker at once.

items.title: Trackers
items.text: Read Sentry errors with stack trace, breadcrumbs and tags inside Goodboy. Comment, assign, edit and move issues in Linear and Jira the same way.

items.title: Code hosts
items.text: Work on GitHub pull requests, GitLab merge requests and Bitbucket comments, approvals and merges without leaving Goodboy. GitHub and GitLab can work side by side.

items.title: Slack: what agents can do
items.text: Choose the channels agents follow and set what each action may do. They never start conversations or send direct messages.

items.title: Reply ready for #channel
items.text: A Slack reply waits in the session as a card with the draft. Send it, edit it or discard it.

items.title: Slack signature
items.text: Show when an agent wrote a Slack reply, with a note you can reword or switch off.

items.title: Images from your tools
items.text: See screenshots attached in Linear, Jira and GitHub inside Goodboy. Your key goes only to that tool's own image host.

items.title: Records read the same way
items.text: Items from any tool read the same way: one list of labels and values, with who opened them and when.

items.title: Comment threads
items.text: Follow replies under the comment they answer, in Linear and GitLab. Long threads fold behind a Show earlier replies link.

items.title: Artifacts
items.text: Plans, reports and wireframes live next to the task, each tagged by kind. Tabs filter the list and each row shows its state.

items.title: Plan parts and Run plan
items.text: Give each part of a plan done-when checks and the files it expects to touch. Run plan turns each part into a sub-agent.

items.title: Report as a document
items.text: Read a report as one document with an outline on the left, and edit the text in place. The same file opens in a browser on another machine.

items.title: Files on disk
items.text: Open any artifact as a folder, in your browser or file manager. The folder is rewritten on each revision.

items.title: Create a wireframe
items.text: Describe the screen in a brief, add attachments, and choose the fidelity and the target: phone, desktop or both. See exactly what goes in the context pack.

items.title: Wireframes scouted first
items.text: Two scouts read your repo before drawing, one for screens and one for data. Every claim must cite a real file.

items.title: Wireframe versions
items.text: Go back to any wireframe version with View, Compare and Restore.

items.title: Compare
items.text: See what changed between two wireframe versions side by side, with a change list under the frames.

items.title: Ask for a change
items.text: Point at what you want changed. Pick elements on the wireframe, choose this screen or all screens, and ask.

items.title: Import wireframe JSON
items.text: Bring in a wireframe made elsewhere, with a preview of any fixes before it lands.

items.title: Revisions and Restore
items.text: Bring back an earlier plan, report or wireframe as a new revision, with its author, without losing the later ones.

items.title: Save a copy and New variant
items.text: Export a wireframe as a folder of pages, or redraw it at the other fidelity.

clusters.title: Providers, limits and cost
clusters.lead: Know how much of each plan is left, keep work moving when one runs out, and see the total bill.

items.title: Usage limits chip
items.text: See how much of your Claude and Codex plans is left before a run stops. Two bars show the 5-hour window and the week.

items.title: Use reset
items.text: When Codex offers a free reset, Goodboy shows it with its expiry. It warns you if using it now would waste most of the week.

items.title: Fallback when a limit is hit
items.text: When a provider runs out, a turn can move to another connected one. The conversation records where it went.

items.title: Fallback order and Auto
items.text: Choose where Auto starts and the order it falls back through. Each role can use Auto or be pinned to a model.

items.title: Model picker
items.text: Pick a model with the reason next to it. The picker leads with Auto and shows what it resolves to right now.

items.title: Impact
items.text: See what Goodboy got done and what it cost over 7 days, 30 days or all time. Tiles compare each figure with the period before.

items.title: Monthly cap and budget alert
items.text: Set a monthly cap per provider and a share of it where Goodboy warns you. Past that, the next turn goes to another provider with room.

clusters.title: Work with agents directly
clusters.lead: Ask questions, give each helper a job, and steer it from the keyboard or a real terminal.

items.title: Workspace chat
items.text: Ask about your repos without starting a session. The answer reads every project and never changes a file, and you can turn it into work later.

items.title: Roles
items.text: Nine roles come with the app, from Scout to Generalist. A role sets the agent's instructions, its default model and what it hands back. When one recommends the next, its reason and result travel with it.

items.title: Agent suggests
items.text: When one agent recommends the next, its reason and result travel with it. Pick the provider, model and effort, then press Start.

items.title: Agent header
items.text: Read who an agent is at a glance. Role, status, time and model sit on one line under the title.

items.title: What the agent received
items.text: Check exactly what an agent was told, with a chip for each part of its brief. View the exact text sent to the provider.

items.title: Agent transcript
items.text: Follow one agent's work in order. Plans and reports show as chips, file edits group together, and questions appear where you answer them.

items.title: Queue or send now
items.text: Keep talking while an agent works. Enter queues your message for its next turn, and ⌘Enter sends it now.

items.title: Stop and Continue
items.text: Stopping keeps what the agent wrote and offers Continue. An agent working during a restart picks up where it stopped.

items.title: Turn footer
items.text: See what each turn cost: provider, model, duration, tokens, cache share, estimated cost and a context meter.

items.title: Tool call states
items.text: Tell at a glance what a tool call did: running, done, failed, needs approval, stopped or denied.

items.title: Composer plus menu
items.text: The plus button attaches files, runs a script, starts a workflow or asks another agent.

items.title: Attach files
items.text: Hand an agent images, PDFs, CSV and text files, up to 10 at a time, by paste, drop or pick.

items.title: Drift warning
items.text: Get a notification when an agent steps outside its role, like a planner editing files.

items.title: Subagents from plan parts
items.text: Run a plan part by part. An implementer splits a plan into one sub-agent per part.

items.title: History rewriter and Scribe
items.text: The helpers that rewrite history and write pull request text cannot push. Their push address goes nowhere and their GitHub tokens are removed.

items.title: One language per session
items.text: Get agents and summaries in the language of your goal.

items.title: Terminal
items.text: Open a real login shell in the session's worktree. It is still there after a reload.

items.title: Keyboard shortcuts, back and forward
items.text: Drive Goodboy from the keyboard with 57 shortcuts. ⌘/ opens the list, and ⌘[ and ⌘] move through history.

items.title: Script drawer
items.text: Watch a script's live output in a drawer. Stop it, run it again and copy the output.

items.title: Open in editor
items.text: Jump into VS Code, Cursor, Zed, the JetBrains IDEs, Sublime Text, Vim or Neovim, at the worktree or the file.

items.title: Explore
items.text: Browse the session folder as a file tree with a preview. Ask an agent about the selected file from its row.

clusters.title: Storage, backup and updates
clusters.lead: Free disk space safely, move your setup between Macs, and keep tokens out of what you save.

items.title: Worktree folders
items.text: See the checkout folders of archived or deleted sessions with their size and whether they are safe to remove. One button clears the clean ones.

items.title: Branches
items.text: Local branches are sorted into safe to delete and needs a look. Every deletion can be restored for 14 days.

items.title: Storage scope
items.text: Clean up this workspace, other workspaces, removed ones or all of them. Bulk actions name the scope they act on.

items.title: Free space chip
items.text: Once at least 1 GB of worktree folders can go, the top bar shows how much. Click it to open Storage.

items.title: Artifacts from deleted sessions
items.text: Decide what to keep from sessions you deleted: their plans, reports and wireframes.

items.title: Goodboy can free N GB
items.text: Hear about reclaimable space once, when idle folders pass 10 GB or the disk runs low. It waits 14 days before speaking again.

items.title: Security findings
items.text: Each time you save a project script, Goodboy checks it for keys and tokens on your Mac. You can dismiss a finding or flag it again.

items.title: Findings kept out of the export
items.text: An export leaves out any script that holds a flagged token, unless you include it on purpose.

items.title: Export and import your setup
items.text: Move your setup to another Mac or keep a copy, in groups you choose. Import shows what it adds before writing anything.

items.title: Backup before a data update
items.text: Before an update changes your data, Goodboy makes a full copy and keeps the last two. If the copy fails, the update does not start.

items.title: Newer data guard
items.text: An older Goodboy opened on newer data stops before touching anything. It offers Restore backup or Quit.

items.title: Updates
items.text: Updates download in the background, then a pill in the top bar offers to restart. With agents running, it can wait until they finish.

items.title: Changelog in the app
items.text: Read release notes inside the app, searchable, with links to the screen each change touched. See what an update brings before you install it.

items.title: Before and after pictures
items.text: Release notes can show Before and After pictures, with a lightbox, in light and dark.

items.title: Guide
items.text: Learn how Goodboy works in 18 short chapters that follow a task. Open Guide from the palette.

items.title: Report a bug
items.text: Press ⌘I from any screen to report a bug in one line. What gets sent is shown first, and secrets, paths and emails are stripped.

items.title: Update pill
items.text: A single light sweep shows when an update is ready.
